name: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-sglang
description: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (552B MoE, 8B prefill / 16B decode CED split, FP8 dense + FP4 routed experts, ~510GB checkpoint, FP4 KV, native 1M ctx, vision) with SGLang TP4/EP4 on 4xH200 - day-0 PREVIEW image lmsysorg/sglang:dev-dsv41, here PINNED BY DIGEST (preview tags move; this digest is the verified one). VERIFIED WORKING 2026-09-14 on that digest with AUTO backends - startup log resolves attention=dsv4 (page_size 256, c128_page_size 16), MoE runner=flashinfer_mxfp4 (quant_method=Mxfp4FlashinferCutlassMoEMethod), multimodal=fa3; served 187k-token agentic requests end-to-end. HISTORY: an earlier 2026-09-14 attempt hit an mxfp4_flashinfer_cutlass TP4 kernel guard (intermediate_size_per_partition=576 not a multiple of 128) and used --moe-runner-backend triton + --speculative-moe-runner-backend triton as a workaround - that workaround is NOT needed on the digest above and must not be carried forward. RECOMMENDED DEFAULT: Engram offloaded via SGLANG_ENABLE_DSV41_ENGRAM_HOST_TABLE=1 - verified 48341 MiB/layer/rank, 100% huge-page backed (THP; the node reports 0 hugetlbfs, THP supplies the 2MB pages) and pinned, which is the precondition the docs require for a cheap gather. Keeps ~46GiB/GPU of HBM for KV and removes 2 Engram all-reduces per step; cost is ~202GB host RAM and a longer load. The host gather is NOT a perf problem: ~200MB per 8192-token chunk over PCIe is <1% of chunk time. mem-fraction-static 0.8 (verified: 0.7 boots with ~41GB/GPU free after pool alloc and ~37GB at DSpark graph capture; step to 0.85 only after a soak). chunked-prefill-size 16384 is the recommended step up from the verified 8192 - it sits exactly at the existing max_prefill_tokens=16384 cap, adds ~1-3GB of activations (ample headroom), and should buy a few percent from better GEMM efficiency; it is NOT the prefill fix (chunk time is already ~fully explained by compute at the observed rate) and it doubles the prefill quantum a concurrent decode can wait behind. Going to 32768 would also require --max-prefill-tokens and is not worth it. Do NOT pass --kv-cache-dtype: MEASURED with fp8_e4m3 the pool costs ~3.5KB/token (187,648 tokens = 0.02 of a 9.38M pool) vs the model's native ~890B/token FP4 - the override burns ~4x KV capacity for no measured compute win. Keep SGLANG_DSV4_COMPRESS_STATE_DTYPE=bf16 (same lever that took V4-Flash from 6.63M to 9.65M tokens). Auto backends - do NOT override --attention-backend/--moe-runner-backend/--fp8-gemm-backend: dsv4 attention and flashinfer_mxfp4 MoE are both INFERRED from the checkpoint (log: 'Use dsv4 attention backend for DeepseekV4ForCausalLM, setting page_size to 256'), so passing them only risks a worse fallback. Mandatory deepseek-v41 parsers (V4 parsers silently emit raw DSML in content). DSPARK has no steps/block knobs. Sampling defaults: edit the MOUNTED generation_config.json for top_p=0.95 (--preferred-sampling-params does not win in this build). MEASURED PERF 2026-09-14 (187k-token prompt, 1 stream): prefill 6.4k tok/s at short ctx decaying to ~2.8k at 180k ctx = 53s prefill + ~10s tokenize (~64s TTFT); decode 62-127 tok/s, DSpark accept len 2.3-4.7 (rate 0.26-0.73). Same box/conversation on GLM-5.3-Flash at 153k ctx: 94-140 tok/s decode - so V4.1 is ~1.3-1.5x off on long-ctx decode but ~2.5x off on PREFILL (6.4k vs ~16k). OPEN ISSUE (upstream, not flags): startup warns 'Using default W8A8 Block FP8 kernel config. Performance might be sub-optimal! Config file not found at .../configs/N=5120,K=15360,device_name=NVIDIA_H200_NVL,dtype=fp8_w8a8,block_shape=[32,32].json' (and N=1536,K=5120) - the preview build ships no tuned H200 configs for the ue8m0 32-wide block shapes, so dense GEMMs run on Triton defaults; prime suspect for the prefill gap and not tunable locally. GOTCHAS: (1) PCAI caps ISvc/deployment names at 63 chars - keep names short ('deepseek-v41-flash', not 'deepseek-v41-flash-engram-offload-predictor-...'); (2) a new pod that begins weight load while a predecessor's TP ranks are still tearing down OOMs in create_weights (process ~64GB, GPU full) - the restart seconds later loads clean, so stagger pod generations and let the old pod fully drain; (3) HiCache dropped (device pool ample); (4) host-RAM need is the pinned Engram copy (~202GB) + anon, so the 512Gi limit is adequate (the ~512GiB transient during load is reclaimable page cache of the 510GB checkpoint and clears itself).
